subject: KV ownership ledger + CAIQ compact — evidence & next steps
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novacorp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: AuditOps Team <audits@auditops.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: compact CAIQ extract + KV ownership ledger for procurement review

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for taking time with our procurement team yesterday. As discussed, Novacorp's InfoSec group needs two compact artifacts to close our tooling review this week: a CAIQ extract that highlights controls mapped to runtime key custody/encryption, and a concise ledger of third-party ownership for any KV/prefix cache or key-value layer used by Redwood's serving runtime.

Specifically we need:
- a CAIQ CSV or PDF with the control IDs and short rationale for runtime/KMS-related items
- a single-table ledger listing each KV/sidecar/managed cache component, owning team/vendor, data residency (region), whether ephemeral keys are used, and the last attestation date

Can you provide these by Friday (2026-09-03) so our SOC 2 review board can greenlight the procurement? If you have a short remediation/mitigation note for any non-covered items, please include it.

Appreciate it — Laura

[Attachment: procurement-checklist-template.xlsx (Excel, 18 KB)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, AuditOps Team <audits@auditops.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: compact CAIQ extract + KV ownership ledger for procurement review

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask. I've pulled together a compact deliverable set and a short mutual action plan so your SOC 2 board has context. High-level notes below; attachments included: caiq-compact-extract.pdf and kv-ownership-ledger.csv (CSV export of our internal ledger).

Highlights:
- CAIQ extract: focuses on controls related to key management (CM-01/ISK equivalents), runtime encryption in transit/at-rest, and access controls for caching layers. We annotated each control with the owner and the evidence artifact we reference (SOC 2 control excerpt, KMS key policy snippets).
- KV ownership ledger: single CSV with columns: component_id, component_name, owner (team/vendor), hosting_region, key_custody_model (redwood-kms / customer-kms / thirdparty), ephemeral_key (yes/no), last_attested (YYYY-MM-DD), evidence_link (Drive id).

Open items / clarifications:
1) A small subset of managed caches (3 entries) are operated by our marketplace partner (CacheFast). We can provide their attestation, but the attestation window is rolling — their next audit is in Q4.
2) For encrypting ephemeral keys we rely on our ephemeral key broker; the broker issues short-lived wrapping keys. Sean (cc'd) can provide a one-page technical excerpt if you need cryptographic details.

Timeline:
- Included attachments are the first pass. If you need formal affidavits or partner attestations packaged, we can get that within 5 business days after you confirm which artifacts are required for your board.

Attachments:
- [kv-ownership-ledger.csv (CSV, 38 KB)]
- [caiq-compact-extract.pdf (PDF, 72 KB)]
- [soc2-control-excerpt.txt (TXT, 9 KB)]

Next step: please confirm if the procurement board accepts the compact extract as-is or if they'd prefer a full CAIQ matrix.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Laura / Vanessa — quick technical clarifications below, in case your board asks for concrete evidence pointers: 

- KV components: the ledger lists 'request-kv-v1' (in-house), 'prefetch-cache' (CacheFast, vendor), and 'session-kv' (managed by Redwood infra team). For CacheFast entries we have a partner attestation PDF; I'll pull the signed attestation into the Drive link referenced in the CSV.
- Key custody: "redwood-kms" entries mean keys are under Redwood's customer-scoped KMS (HSM-backed, multi-tenant but logically isolated). "customer-kms" means we integrate with the customer's external KMS via a key-wrapping flow.
- Evidence pointers: SOC 2 excerpt (attached) includes control IDs and test sample references. The caiq-compact includes the specific artifact IDs.

If Novacorp needs a short cryptographic note (1 page) describing the ephemeral wrapping flow and rotation cadence (30-60s token lifetime, 24h rotation for service keys), I can produce that and add the signed statement to the Drive folder.

-Sean
